name: Kawasaki KZ650
engine: 652 cc air-cooled DOHC inline four, four carbs
intro: A light, quick DOHC four. Cheap to buy, well supported, and mostly let down by tired ignition parts and old rubber.
focus: Leaks come one at a time

add.title: Get JIS screwdriver bits
add.instructions: The cross-head screws on the KZ are JIS, not Phillips. Buy a set of JIS bits before you touch the engine covers or carbs.
add.reason: Phillips bits cam out and strip JIS screws, which turns a 5-minute job into drilling out screws.

add.title: Service the points and auto advancer
add.instructions: On points bikes, fit new Kawasaki points and condenser, set the gap, and free up the automatic timing advancer under the right-hand cover. Then set the timing.
add.reason: Worn points and a sticky advancer cause misfires and flat spots that look like carb trouble.

add.title: Check the clutch cushion rubbers
add.instructions: With the clutch apart, check the rubber dampers in the clutch basket. After a few decades they break up.
add.reason: Broken cushion rubbers make the clutch rattle and clunk.

add.title: Track down o-ring leaks
add.instructions: Clean the engine and find each leak at its source. Many come from the engine's rubber o-rings, which age out one at a time.
add.reason: Fixing the right o-ring beats chasing the same leak across the cases.

A: Buy the Kawasaki service manual. Owners on KZRider point new restorers to it first.
G: Keep each carb's parts in a container marked with its number.

recallNote: Any recalls on bikes this old were closed long ago.

known.title: Points ignition
known.what: Worn points and a sticky advancer cause high-rpm misfires.

known.title: Rubber o-ring leaks
known.what: Many small o-rings in the engine fail one at a time.

known.title: Clutch cushion rubbers
known.what: Dampers in the clutch break up with age.

known.title: Varnished carbs
known.what: Bikes that sat often start only on choke until the jets are cleaned.
